paragraphs: Mia visited May's house on Sunday afternoon. May and her brother Pat lived in the white house next to the school. "Let's play a game," said Mia. "I can guess what Pat likes most." "It is easy," said May, "but Pat does not know the game." Pat was in the garden. He was eight, and he often played alone there. Mia and May sat on the steps.

First, Mia looked at Pat's clothes. His T-shirt had a big yellow butterfly on the front. His hat had a small blue butterfly on it too. His shoes were green, and his socks were yellow. "What a lovely hat!" said Mia. "Perhaps he likes butterflies." "But I need to see more," she said. "Perhaps someone gave him these clothes." May smiled and said nothing.

Then the girls watched Pat in the garden. Flowers of many colors were all around him. The sun was warm, and the grass was green. He saw a beetle and a snail, but he did not stay long. A butterfly came over the flowers, and Pat stopped. The butterfly flew up to a high branch. Pat stood on his toes and looked up. He did not move for a long time. "It is beautiful," he said quietly.

"I know!" said Mia. "You like butterflies most, Pat." "How do you know?" asked Pat. "I know because you stopped only for the butterfly," said Mia. Pat laughed. "Yes!" he said. "They are the most beautiful insects." "I have a book about them," he said. "Wait here!" Pat ran to get his butterfly book. Mia guessed right, and Pat was very happy.
text.summary: Mia plays a guessing game at May's house. She looks at Pat's clothes and watches him in the garden, and then she guesses what he likes most.
